sections.title: The letter El
paragraphs: The letter is named (El) /ɛl/. Its main sound is heard in (Lampe) /ˈlampə/, which means lamp. This letter makes only one sound. A consonant is a sound made when the mouth narrows the air. This consonant always stays clear and bright in every word.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: Touch the ridge behind your upper teeth with your tongue tip. Keep the back of your tongue low and flat. Let the air flow smoothly around the sides of your tongue. A lateral is a consonant where the air flows along the sides of the tongue. Turn your voice on. Voiced means your voice is on. Place a hand on your throat to feel it shake.

sections.title: Reading this letter
paragraphs: This letter always makes the sound /l/. You hear it at the start of a word in (Lampe) /ˈlampə/. You hear the same sound at the end of a word in (Ball) /bal/. A double consonant is written as two of the same letter. The double letter in (Ball) /bal/ makes that same single sound.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not pull the back of your tongue up toward the roof of your mouth. In English, the end of ball sounds dark and heavy. Keep the back of your tongue flat and low. Keep the tongue tip firm behind your upper teeth.
